subject: Peter Murrell jailed for more than five years for embezzling SNP funds
posts:
A former party executive faces justice for financial crimes.

Peter Murrell jailed for more than five years for embezzling SNP funds
Evidence: stated crime, actual conviction, actual consequence

Peter Murrell, former chief executive of the SNP and estranged husband of Nicola Sturgeon, has been sentenced to over five years in prison for embezzling more than £400,000 from the party.
Stated Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Murrell admitted to embezzling £400,310.65 from the SNP between 2010 and 2022, using party funds for personal purchases. He has been sentenced to five years and three months, with his sentence backdated.
Stated Judgement: (-1.5, -1.5) — Greater Evil

Verdict: PASS — Reckoning into Destruction.
Murrell's conviction and sentencing represent a direct consequence of his actions, fulfilling the 'reckoning' for his embezzlement and leading to 'destruction' of his freedom and reputation.

Peter Murrell, the former SNP chief executive, has been sentenced to over five years in jail after admitting to embezzling over £400,000 from the party. He used the funds for personal items, and the investigation began after questions about referendum funds.
